title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Withdrawal by the Shipper
content:
## Clause

Withdrawing a Dangerous Goods Acceptance application, or goods that have already been approved, is something only the shipper can do, and it can be done only while the goods have not been loaded. A withdrawal made before approval costs nothing. Withdrawing approved goods brings the category's withdrawal fee, charged once; the administration fee charged with the approval remains payable, and no surcharge arises, as nothing went on board. Goods already loaded can no longer be withdrawn.

Two record conditions govern the withdrawal fee: it can be entered only on an acceptance whose status is withdrawn, and a single acceptance never carries more than one withdrawal fee.

## Status grid

| Status at the moment of withdrawal | Withdrawal open to the shipper | Withdrawal fee | Administration fee from an approval | Loading surcharges |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| submitted | yes | none | — | none |
| under review | yes | none | — | none |
| approved | yes | category fee, once | stays payable | none |
| loaded | no | — | — | — |

## Points of judgement

**Who can instruct the withdrawal?** The shipper alone; the desk does not withdraw goods on its own initiative.

**The shipper withdrew approved goods; is the administration fee refunded?** No. It stays payable, and the withdrawal fee is added once.

**Can a second withdrawal fee arise on the same acceptance?** No; one acceptance carries at most one.
